summary: Karma Ura works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at St. Stephen's College, Magdalen College, and the University of Edinburgh, and served as Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH from 1999 to 2008.

Karsé Kongtrul studied under Shechen Gyaltsab, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, the 13th Dalai Lama, and Khakyab Dorje. His students included Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Gangshar.

Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University, and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Karunesh Shukla is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation (attested 1991). He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1991).

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz works in Tibetology, religious studies, and Central Asian studies. She studied and completed her PhD and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, and became a professor (1999) and faculty dean (2007–2010) at the University of Bern.

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Allahabad, Jesus College, Oxford, and Lincoln's Inn. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta (1917) and president of the Numismatic Society of India.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit was an archaeologist and Indologist. He held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and served as Director General of Archaeology at the Archaeological Survey of India from 1937 to 1944, succeeding Rakhal Das Banerji.

Kashinath Trimbak Telang was an Indologist who studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai under Narayan Mahadev Parmanand. He served at Elphinstone College, as syndic and vice-chancellor of the University of Mumbai, and as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar was an Indologist and linguist who taught Masaaki Hattori. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Arts & Science College (~1922–1945) and Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1957).

Kate Crosby is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She held posts at Cardiff University (attested 2002), the Buddhist Institute (2003), and the Seiyu Kiriyama post in Buddhist Studies at SOAS University of London.
Kate Wharton works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London by 2008 and held an attested post at Birkbeck, University of London, in 2010.
Katharina Sabernig works in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from the University of Vienna by 2017 and held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.

Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned a Master of Arts degree at McGill University, where she studied under MA supervisor G. Victor Sōgen Hori (attested 2008).

Katherine Anne Paul is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and archaeologist. Her doctoral supervisor was Gudrun Bühnemann, and she also studied under teachers Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Paul J. Griffiths, also studying under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She completed an M.A. at the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. at McGill University (~1970–1978), where she also served as Professor (~1978).
Katherine Verdery studied at Reed College (~1966–1970) and Stanford University (~1970–1977). She held a post at the City University of New York (~2005).

Kathleen D. Morrison is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley, later holding posts at Northwestern University (~1993–1995) and the University of Pennsylvania (~2017).

Kathleen Kenyon was an archaeologist who studied at St Paul's Girls' School and Somerville College, Oxford. She held posts at the UCL Institute of Archaeology and the University of London (1948–1962), and later at St Hugh's College (1962–1973).

Kathleen M. Erndl specialized in Indology and religious studies. She held academic posts at DePauw University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, Lewis & Clark College (~1987–1993), and Florida State University (~1993–2017).
